q: Matter is composed of ____ which are very small in size.
e: Matter is composed of atoms which are very small in size. The physics in this sentence is built around atoms.

q: An atom consists of a core called the ____ around which the particles called electrons are moving in orbits.
e: An atom consists of a core called the nucleus around which the particles called electrons are moving in orbits. Nucleus here means the tiny positive core of an atom, protons and neutrons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: An electron is a negatively charged particle having a charge of ____ C.
e: An electron is a negatively charged particle having a charge of $-1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C. The physics in this sentence is built around $-1.6 \times 10^{-19}$.

q: The nucleus consists of two kinds of particles called proton and ____.
e: The nucleus consists of two kinds of particles called proton and neutron. Neutron here means the uncharged nucleon inside the nucleus. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: A proton is a positively charged particle and a neutron is an ____ particle.
e: A proton is a positively charged particle and a neutron is an uncharged particle. The physics in this sentence is built around uncharged.

q: An electron and a proton have the same ____ of electric charge.
e: An electron and a proton have the same magnitude of electric charge. The physics in this sentence is built around magnitude.

q: The magnitude of positive charge of the nucleus is equal to the sum of the positive charges of all the protons present in the ____.
e: The magnitude of positive charge of the nucleus is equal to the sum of the positive charges of all the protons present in the nucleus. Nucleus here means the tiny positive core of an atom, protons and neutrons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: In a normal atom the number of orbiting electrons is always equal to the number of ____.
e: In a normal atom the number of orbiting electrons is always equal to the number of protons. The physics in this sentence is built around protons.

q: Since the magnitude of positive charge of the nucleus is equal to that of the total negative charge of electrons, a normal atom has no ____ charge.
e: Since the magnitude of positive charge of the nucleus is equal to that of the total negative charge of electrons, a normal atom has no net charge. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: It is said to be electrically ____.
e: It is said to be electrically neutral. The physics in this sentence is built around neutral.

q: If an atom gains one or more electrons, it carries a ____ charge.
e: If an atom gains one or more electrons, it carries a negative charge. The physics in this sentence is built around negative.

q: If an atom loses one or more electrons, it becomes ____ charged.
e: If an atom loses one or more electrons, it becomes positively charged. The physics in this sentence is built around positively.

q: When an atom becomes a charged atom, it is called an ____.
e: When an atom becomes a charged atom, it is called an ion. Ion names when an atom becomes a charged atom, it.
